questions.q: According to this lesson, why does a newly deployed environment with no monitoring configured count as "flying blind"?
options: Nobody will know anything is wrong until it's noticed the hard way, even though resources are running and traffic is flowing
Azure and AWS refuse to run resources until monitoring is configured
Platform metrics don't exist until monitoring is manually turned on
Flying blind only applies to environments with no network configured
questions.explain: The resources run and traffic flows, but with no monitoring, problems stay invisible until someone notices the hard way.

questions.q: In the disk-fills-up example, what is the actual difference between the "with monitoring" and "without monitoring" outcomes?
options: The root cause is identical; the only difference is whether the problem was caught from an alert in advance or from a user complaint after a crash
Monitoring prevents the disk from ever filling up in the first place
Without monitoring, the disk fills up faster
The two scenarios have completely different root causes
questions.explain: Both scenarios start from the same slow disk fill — monitoring only changes whether the team finds out in advance or after the damage.

questions.q: What does this lesson say already happens automatically once VMs/EC2 instances and storage are deployed?
options: Platform metrics start being collected automatically, with no setup required
Alerts automatically notify the team of any problem
Logs are automatically centralized into a workspace or log group
Nothing happens automatically until monitoring is explicitly configured
questions.explain: Platform metrics collection starts the moment a resource exists, exactly as covered earlier in this program — but nothing is watching or alerting on them yet.

questions.q: What three gaps does "standing up monitoring" concretely close, according to this lesson?
options: A log destination to collect into, visibility into existing metrics, and a place for alerts to land
A bigger VM, more storage, and a faster network connection
A new resource group, a new subscription, and a new region
A backup policy, a restore test, and a disaster recovery plan
questions.explain: The platform already collects metrics; what's missing is a log destination, visibility into that data, and somewhere alerts can land.

questions.q: What is the first concrete monitoring step this lesson recommends taking right after the smoke test?
options: Creating the Log Analytics workspace (Azure) or CloudWatch Log group (AWS) that everything else will attach to
Immediately configuring alerts on every available metric
Resizing the VM or EC2 instance to a larger size
Deleting the smoke-test resources before continuing
questions.explain: Every diagnostic extension, agent, and alert configured later in this chapter points at this log destination, so it's created first.
